# Prime Ministers of Sweden — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/swedish-prime-ministers.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/swedish-prime-ministers.ttl`](../decks/swedish-prime-ministers.ttl) · **Cards:** 35 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

All 35 prime ministers of Sweden, from Louis De Geer, the first in 1876, to Ulf Kristersson, who was still in office on 4 October 2026 (Östen Undén's five days as acting prime minister in 1946 are not counted). Front: the prime minister's name; back: the years of each term, several terms separated by commas ("1969–1976, 1982–1986"). A note gives the party where the sources agree on it, and sometimes a short fact. Taken from Wikidata and checked against the Government Offices' list of prime ministers (regeringen.se) and the Riksdag.

## Licensing

The only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection of prime ministers, the years of every term, the names, the party notes and the other note facts come from it, so the deck can be CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. The Government Offices' list and article (regeringen.se) and the Riksdag's notices (riksdagen.se), whose text carries no open licence, and the Swedish and English Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts the Wikidata data gave and decided which party notes are uncontested; no wording, table or selection was copied from them. Two points were checked against the builder's rule that a verification source contributes no text. First, Ulf Kristersson's caretaker government in the autumn of 2026 is given only by regeringen.se and riksdagen.se, so it is not on the card: his note says only that he was in office from 18 October 2022 and still on 4 October 2026 (Wikidata: no end time), which those sources confirm. Second, three parties have no English label in Wikidata; their English names in the notes (Freeminded People's Party, Farmers' League, People's Party) are the compiler's translations of the Wikidata Swedish labels, and the English Wikipedia only confirmed that they are the names in established English use. A party's name is a short name, not protectable expression, so even where it coincides with a source's wording nothing protected is copied. The Swedish notes are in the compiler's own words; the short phrases "Sveriges första statsminister" and "Sveriges första kvinnliga statsminister" coincide with the Government Offices' text because they are the only natural way to say those facts. The selection is every holder of the office, which coincides with any complete list because it is the complete set, not a choice taken from a list; leaving out Östen Undén's acting term follows the Government Offices' count, a convention, not text. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence are not part of the CC0 deck: they remain under their sources' terms (Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0, by Wikipedia contributors, each linked to the quoted revision; the Government Offices' and the Riksdag's text without a stated licence) and are short quotations given only to make the verification checkable.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. The prime ministers and their terms (query 1): every statement P39 (position held) = Prime Minister of Sweden (Q687075), of all ranks, with its start time (P580), end time (P582), replaces/replaced by (P1365/P1366) qualifiers and the English and Swedish labels of the person. It returned 48 statements for 38 items. Two items have no start or end time and are fictional characters (P31 fictional human, Q15632617, query 4): Q131546077 "Erland" (en alias "Hedenhös Erland") and Q131566167 (mul label "Thorbjörn Fälldin", en alias "Whiskey on the Rocks Thorbjörn Fälldin", a film character); they were left out. The other 46 statements are the 45 terms of 35 prime ministers plus Östen Undén's acting term (6–11 October 1946), each with a start time and, except Ulf Kristersson's, an end time; the chain of P1365/P1366 qualifiers is unbroken from Louis De Geer to Ulf Kristersson.
3. Backs: for each prime minister the terms are written as years, in order and separated by ", ": "start–end", the single year when a term began and ended in the same year ("1905"), and "2022–" for the term still running. Terms are counted as Wikidata and the Government Offices count them: Per Albin Hansson's two terms (1932–1936, 1936–1946) are separate because Axel Pehrsson-Bramstorp was prime minister in the summer of 1936; Hjalmar Branting's three terms are separate; Stefan Löfven's 2014–2021 is one term in both sources. Because two backs are the same (Johan Ramstedt and Christian Lundeberg were both prime minister only in 1905), the deck is studied front to back only.
4. Cross-check against the Government Offices (queries 6, 15 and 17): the page "Statsministerämbetet" on regeringen.se lists "Sveriges statsministrar sedan 1876", one entry per term with the years in the heading and the dates of taking and leaving office in the text. The saved HTML was turned into text by removing <script> and <style> elements, replacing every other tag by a line break, decoding HTML entities and dropping empty lines. After the line "Sveriges statsministrar sedan 1876", every line of the form "Name (years)" (regular expression ^(.+?) \((\d{4}(?:–\d{4}|–)?)\)$) starts an entry, and the entry's first paragraph is the next non-empty line that is not a photo credit ("Foto: …"). This gave 45 entries for 35 names. The entries of each name, in page order, were joined with ", " and compared with the back computed from Wikidata (query 1, Östen Undén left out): "start–end" in years, the single year when both are the same, "start–" when there is no end time, terms in order of start time, joined with ", ". regeringen.se writes "Karl Staff" for Karl Staaff, so that one name was mapped by hand. For every prime minister the two agree, and every entry was matched to exactly one card. The authoring run used two scratch scripts (extract.py and make_dossier.py, query 15) that did this and wrote the cards; they were not kept in the repository, so in quality-control round 3 the comparison was re-implemented as the self-contained script given verbatim in query 17, run on the same saved page and Wikidata result, with the same outcome (45 entries, 35 names, every back equal). Each card's evidence quotes the heading and the first paragraph of each entry. The dates in the text agree with Wikidata's start and end times except for two typing errors on regeringen.se (Åkerhielm's start given as 1989 and Ekman's as 1925; see quality control), Rickard Sandler's start date given without a year ("den 24 januari"), and Ingvar Carlsson's start (see below). Dates in the page's lists of government compositions (such as "13 december 1939 – 31 juli 1945") mark changes of coalition within a term, not terms, and were not compared.
5. The 2026 cut-off: Sweden held a general election in September 2026. Wikidata's P39 statement for Ulf Kristersson has a start time (2022-10-18) and no end time (queries 1 and 20, re-checked on 4 October 2026). On 4 October 2026 the regeringen.se front page (query 7) said "Sedan den 17 september har Sverige en övergångsregering som leds av statsminister Ulf Kristersson", and its article of 17 September (query 8) said that the Speaker had dismissed the prime minister at his own request but that he and the other ministers stay in office until a new government takes office. The Riksdag's notices of 17 September and 2 October 2026 (queries 10 and 11) confirm the request and say that Magdalena Andersson's sounding-out runs until 12 October at the latest and that the vote on a new prime minister follows it; the Riksdag's news page on 4 October 2026 (query 18) lists no such vote. The card therefore gives "2022–" and its note says only that he was prime minister since 18 October 2022 and still in office on 4 October 2026; the description states that cut-off. The caretaker status itself is given only by the verification sources, so it is recorded in the selection and the quality control, not on the card. Wikidata's item for the Kristersson government (Q114671310, query 20) has no end or caretaker statement either.
6. Names (query 3): the fronts are the English and Swedish labels of the prime ministers, which are the same in both languages (personal names are not translated in Swedish or English usage; Ulf Kristersson's item has no Swedish label, only an English and a multilingual (mul) label, which the builder accepts). The exception is the two Louis De Geers, father (prime minister 1876–1880) and son (1920–1921), whose names are the same: the Swedish fronts use the forms of the Government Offices and Wikidata's Swedish aliases, "Louis De Geer d.ä." (den äldre) and "Louis De Geer d.y." (den yngre), and the English fronts "Louis De Geer the Elder" and "Louis De Geer the Younger". The family name is written "De Geer" with a capital D, as the Government Offices, the Swedish and English Wikipedia and Wikidata's aliases write it; Wikidata's labels of the two items write "de Geer" (and the English label of the son is his full name "Gerhard Louis De Geer"), so for these two cards the builder checks the alias "Louis De Geer d.ä." (father), the alias "Louis De Geer (1854–1935)" and the English label (son) rather than the front text.
7. Party notes (query 2): every P102 (member of political party) statement of the prime ministers, with its start and end times and the parties' labels, was compared with the party columns of the Swedish Wikipedia table (revision 59731831, query 13) and the English Wikipedia list (revision 1377756809, query 14). In the 19th and early 20th centuries the Riksdag groups changed often and the sources describe them differently, so a party note was written only where Wikidata has a P102 statement that overlaps the term (or an undated one) and both Wikipedias agree with it for the whole term: 27 of the 35 cards. In one case the statement covers only part of the term: Arvid Posse's only P102 statement (Lantmannapartiet) ends in 1881, partway through his 1880–1883 term; his note is kept because both Wikipedias give Lantmannapartiet for the whole term and no source gives another party (quality-control round 5). No party note was written for Louis De Geer the Elder, Carl Johan Thyselius, Robert Themptander, Gillis Bildt and Louis De Geer the Younger (Wikidata has no party statement covering their terms; both Wikipedias call them independent), Erik Gustaf Boström (Wikidata: the Protectionist Party 1894–1907; the Swedish Wikipedia: Lantmannapartiet for both terms; the English Wikipedia: the Protectionist Party for the first, the Lantmanna Party for the second), Fredrik von Otter (Wikidata's only P102 statement, the Protectionist Party, is deprecated) and Arvid Lindman (Wikidata: the First Chamber Protectionist Party 1905–1909 and the Lantmanna- och borgarepartiet 1912–1934; the Swedish Wikipedia: Lantmanna- och borgarepartiet; the English Wikipedia: Lantmanna Party (General Electoral League) for both terms). The party's Swedish name in the note is its Wikidata Swedish (or multilingual) label; the English name is its Wikidata English label where that is the usual English name (Lantmanna Party, Protectionist Party, National Party, Swedish Social Democratic Party, Centre Party, Moderate Party), the English alias "Liberal Coalition party" (capitalised) for Liberala samlingspartiet, whose label is "Free-minded National Association", and, for the three parties without an English label in Wikidata (query 19: Frisinnade folkpartiet Q4887122, Bondeförbundet Q110472693 and Folkpartiet Q53764745 have only Swedish or multilingual labels, the last also the en label "Folkpartiet (Sweden)"), the compiler's English translation of the Swedish label: Freeminded People's Party (frisinnade = free-minded), Farmers' League (bonde = farmer, förbund = league) and People's Party (folk = people). The English Wikipedia was consulted to confirm that these are the names in established English use; it uses the same three names. In the first draft these names were taken from the English Wikipedia and the Ola Ullsten note added "(Folkpartiet)" in brackets; quality-control rounds 2 and 3 removed the bracket and re-based the names on the Wikidata labels. Johan Ramstedt and Oscar von Sydow are "partilös" (independent politician, Q327591) in Wikidata; Hjalmar Hammarskjöld is "högervilde" (Q111104528, an independent member on the right); a vilde is a member of the Riksdag outside every party group, and Wikidata itself gives "politisk vilde" as a Swedish alias of "partilös" (Q327591, en alias "independent"; query 19); all three are independent in both Wikipedias, and their note says "No party (independent)" / "Partilös".
8. Other notes, in the compiler's own words: the two De Geers' relationship (Wikidata P40/P22, query 4; the Government Offices: "Han var son till Louis De Geer d.ä."); Louis De Geer the Elder the first prime minister (Wikidata: the first P39 statement, 1876; the Government Offices: "Sveriges första statsminister"); the deaths in office of Per Albin Hansson (P570 1946-10-06, the end of his term) and his replacement by Axel Pehrsson-Bramstorp's government from June to September 1936 (the P39 dates of both, query 1) and Olof Palme (P570 1986-02-28, P1196 homicide; query 5), both also in the Government Offices' text; Tage Erlander the longest-serving (23 years, the longest term from query 1; the Government Offices: "den statsminister som suttit längst på posten"; the first draft's Swedish note copied that phrase and was reworded in quality-control round 3); Magdalena Andersson the first woman (P21 female; every earlier holder in query 1 a man; the Government Offices: "Sveriges första kvinnliga statsminister"); and Ulf Kristersson's term still running on 4 October 2026 (above).
9. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata that the person holds the position (P39 Q687075) and the English and Swedish labels of the front (for the De Geers the aliases named above), and for every party note the P102 value and the party's Swedish label (and the English label where the note uses it); plus the note facts P40, P22, P570, P1196 and P21. The builder cannot check qualifiers, so the start and end times were compared by script against the Government Offices' list instead (above, query 17). Hjalmar Hammarskjöld's note is also checked against the aliases "politisk vilde" and "independent" of Q327591. The deck was then validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts).

## Selection

Every Prime Minister of Sweden (statsminister) from the creation of the office on 20 March 1876 to 4 October 2026: 35 people, 45 terms, as the Government Offices count them ("Sedan dess har Sverige haft 35 statsministrar"). One card per person, with all their terms on the back. Left out: Östen Undén, who was acting prime minister (tillförordnad statsminister) for five days after Per Albin Hansson's death in October 1946 and whom the Government Offices do not count (Wikidata has a P39 statement for him; the English Wikipedia lists him as "Acting Prime Minister" without a number); the acting or deputy periods of others (Ingvar Carlsson's first days in 1986 are within his first term's year anyway); the offices before 1876 (justitiestatsminister and utrikesstatsminister); and two fictional characters that Wikidata records as holders of the office. Facts that change or are contested are left out: party notes for the eight early prime ministers whose party affiliation the sources describe differently or Wikidata does not record for the term, and anything about the government formation after the 2026 election beyond the fact that Ulf Kristersson was still in office on 4 October 2026. (He then led a caretaker government, having asked to be dismissed on 17 September 2026; only the Government Offices and the Riksdag, verification sources, say so, so this is recorded here and in quality control but not on the card.)

## Queries

**1. Every P39 Prime Minister of Sweden (Q687075) statement, all ranks, with start/end times, replaces/replaced by and labels (saved as q1.csv)** (Wikidata: holders of the position Prime Minister of Sweden (Q687075), with the start and end times of each term, their political parties (P102) and the labels of the prime ministers and the parties)

```
SELECT ?pm ?pmEn ?pmSv ?stmt ?rank ?start ?end ?party ?partyEn ?partySv ?replaces ?replacedBy WHERE {
  ?pm p:P39 ?stmt .
  ?stmt ps:P39 wd:Q687075 ;
        wikibase:rank ?rank .
  OPTIONAL { ?stmt pq:P580 ?start }
  OPTIONAL { ?stmt pq:P582 ?end }
  OPTIONAL { ?stmt pq:P4100 ?party .
    OPTIONAL { ?party rdfs:label ?partyEn FILTER(LANG(?partyEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?party rdfs:label ?partySv FILTER(LANG(?partySv) = "sv") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?stmt pq:P1365 ?replaces }
  OPTIONAL { ?stmt pq:P1366 ?replacedBy }
  OPTIONAL { ?pm rdfs:label ?pmEn FILTER(LANG(?pmEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?pm rdfs:label ?pmSv FILTER(LANG(?pmSv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?start
```

**2. Party memberships (P102) of the holders, with ranks, start/end times and party labels (q2.csv)** (Wikidata: holders of the position Prime Minister of Sweden (Q687075), with the start and end times of each term, their political parties (P102) and the labels of the prime ministers and the parties)

```
SELECT ?pm ?pmEn ?party ?partyEn ?partySv ?rank ?start ?end WHERE {
  ?pm p:P39/ps:P39 wd:Q687075 .
  ?pm p:P102 ?st .
  ?st ps:P102 ?party ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P580 ?start }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P582 ?end }
  OPTIONAL { ?pm rdfs:label ?pmEn FILTER(LANG(?pmEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?party rdfs:label ?partyEn FILTER(LANG(?partyEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?party rdfs:label ?partySv FILTER(LANG(?partySv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?pmEn ?start
```

**3. English, Swedish and multilingual labels and aliases of the prime ministers, the parties and the two fictional items (q3.csv)** (Wikidata: holders of the position Prime Minister of Sweden (Q687075), with the start and end times of each term, their political parties (P102) and the labels of the prime ministers and the parties)

```
SELECT ?item ?kind ?lang ?text WHERE {
  VALUES ?item { wd:Q52950 wd:Q52951 wd:Q52956 wd:Q52958 wd:Q52960 wd:Q52964 wd:Q52968 wd:Q52969 wd:Q52972 wd:Q53286 wd:Q53292 wd:Q53294 wd:Q53300 wd:Q53305 wd:Q53310 wd:Q53620 wd:Q53626 wd:Q53628 wd:Q53633 wd:Q53637 wd:Q53642 wd:Q53650 wd:Q53660 wd:Q53701 wd:Q298317 wd:Q53707 wd:Q53713 wd:Q53721 wd:Q53733 wd:Q53740 wd:Q52922 wd:Q53747 wd:Q52920 wd:Q2740012 wd:Q4935873 wd:Q1780398 wd:Q6487621 wd:Q7251368 wd:Q327591 wd:Q1594086 wd:Q3480145 wd:Q105112 wd:Q4887122 wd:Q110472693 wd:Q110832 wd:Q53764745 wd:Q110843 wd:Q131546077 wd:Q131566167 }
  VALUES ?lang { "en" "sv" "mul" }
  { ?item rdfs:label ?text . BIND("label" AS ?kind) } UNION { ?item skos:altLabel ?text . BIND("alias" AS ?kind) }
  FILTER(LANG(?text) = ?lang)
}
ORDER BY ?item ?lang ?kind
```

**4. The De Geers' parent/child statements, the class of the two items without dates, Hammarskjöld's P102** (Wikidata: holders of the position Prime Minister of Sweden (Q687075), with the start and end times of each term, their political parties (P102) and the labels of the prime ministers and the parties)

```

**5. Note facts: dates of death, Palme's manner of death, Andersson's P21, the De Geers' dates** (Wikidata: holders of the position Prime Minister of Sweden (Q687075), with the start and end times of each term, their political parties (P102) and the labels of the prime ministers and the parties)

```
SELECT ?item ?p ?v WHERE { VALUES (?item ?p) { (wd:Q53660 wdt:P570) (wd:Q53713 wdt:P570) (wd:Q53713 wdt:P1196) (wd:Q4935873 wdt:P21) (wd:Q52950 wdt:P569) (wd:Q53626 wdt:P569) (wd:Q52950 wdt:P570) (wd:Q53626 wdt:P570)} ?item ?p ?v }

**6. The Government Offices' list of prime ministers since 1876 (saved; turned into text as described in the method and in query 17)** (Statsministerämbetet — Sveriges statsministrar sedan 1876 (regeringen.se))

**17. Quality-control round 3: self-contained re-implementation of the comparison of the regeringen.se headings with Wikidata's terms, run as "python3 compare.py regeringen-statsministerambetet.html q1.csv" on the page saved by query 6 and the result of query 1 (output: 45 entries, 35 names, every back equal)** (Statsministerämbetet — Sveriges statsministrar sedan 1876 (regeringen.se))

```
# Usage: python3 compare.py statsministerambetet.html q1.csv
# Compares the year headings of regeringen.se's "Sveriges statsministrar sedan 1876" with Wikidata's P39 terms.
import csv, html, re, sys
from collections import OrderedDict
page = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()
page = re.sub(r"<(script|style)\b.*?</\1>", "", page, flags=re.S)
lines = [l.strip() for l in html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "\n", page)).split("\n")]
lines = [l for l in lines if l]
i = lines.index("Sveriges statsministrar sedan 1876")
head = re.compile(r"^(.+?) \((\d{4}(?:–\d{4}|–)?)\)$")
reg = OrderedDict()  # name -> [years of each entry, in page order]
for l in lines[i + 1:]:
    m = head.match(l)
    if m:
        reg.setdefault(m.group(1), []).append(m.group(2))
NAME = {"Karl Staff": "Karl Staaff"}  # regeringen.se's spelling -> Wikidata label
wd = OrderedDict()
for r in csv.DictReader(open(sys.argv[2], encoding="utf-8")):
    if r["start"] and r["pmSv"] != "Östen Undén":
        wd.setdefault(r["pmSv"] or r["pmEn"], []).append((r["start"][:4], r["end"][:4]))
def back(terms):
    return ", ".join(s + "–" if not e else s if s == e else f"{s}–{e}" for s, e in terms)
print(sum(len(v) for v in reg.values()), "entries,", len(reg), "names on regeringen.se;", len(wd), "people in Wikidata")
for name, years in reg.items():
    print(NAME.get(name, name), "|", ", ".join(years))
for name, terms in wd.items():
    print("WD", name, "|", back(terms))
```

**22. Quality-control round 4: every day-month(-year) date in the text of the saved regeringen.se list (after "Sveriges statsministrar sedan 1876") compared with the start and end times in the saved Wikidata result q1.csv (query 1); prints dates without a year and dates not found in Wikidata (script qc4_dates.py, verbatim; run as python3 qc4_dates.py)** (Statsministerämbetet — Sveriges statsministrar sedan 1876 (regeringen.se))

```
import csv, re
D = "/tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo--claude-worktrees-authored-decks/0d3ab5ce-8aa3-4420-b0eb-935ec077f401/scratchpad/decks/swedish-prime-ministers/"
M = {m: i + 1 for i, m in enumerate("januari februari mars april maj juni juli augusti september oktober november december".split())}
dates = set()
for r in csv.DictReader(open(D + "q1.csv")):
    for k in ("start", "end"):
        if r[k]:
            dates.add(r[k][:10])
text = open(D + "regeringen-statsministerambetet.txt").read()
text = text[text.index("Sveriges statsministrar sedan 1876"):]
for line in text.splitlines():
    for m in re.finditer(r"(\d{1,2}) (" + "|".join(M) + r")(?: (\d{4}))?", line):
        d, mon, y = m.groups()
        if not y:
            print("NO YEAR:", line[:160])
            continue
        iso = f"{y}-{M[mon]:02d}-{int(d):02d}"
        if iso not in dates:
            print("NOT IN WIKIDATA:", iso, "|", line[:160])

```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 29 findings: 24 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 5 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (186 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every term against Wikidata and the Government Offices' list; every party note against Wikidata and the Swedish and English Wikipedia; the state of the office on 4 October 2026 against regeringen.se and riksdagen.se. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 35 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.

Wikidata and the Government Offices agree on every term of every prime minister (the years of all 45 terms, compared by script); the dates in their text agree except for two typing errors on regeringen.se, Rickard Sandler's start date given without a year, and Ingvar Carlsson's first days in 1986, none of which changes a year. Wikidata includes Östen Undén's acting term and two fictional items, all left out. Party notes were kept only where Wikidata and both Wikipedias agree (27 cards). No Wikidata check was skipped because a better source disagreed; for the De Geers the checks are on aliases because the front text is not a Wikidata label. Builder checks cover P39 for every card, the front labels, the party statements and labels, and the note facts.

### Round 3: Licensing, attribution and documentation (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Licensing, attribution and documentation reviewer · **Scope:** All 35 cards' evidence, every source's licence record, the method, queries, selection and licensing.

Licences are recorded correctly and all quoted strings are verbatim, but four warnings and one suggestion were raised, all accepted: text from verification sources in the Kristersson note and in three English party names, a Swedish phrase copied from regeringen.se, a method that depended on unpublished scripts, and news results mentioned without being listed. The Kristersson note was cut to what Wikidata supports, the English party names were re-based on the Wikidata Swedish labels (and Hammarskjöld's note on Wikidata's own vilde/partilös alias), the Erlander note reworded, the comparison script published verbatim in query 17, and query 16 corrected.

|---|---|---|---|

The note was cut to what Wikidata supports and the verification sources confirm: en "Party: Moderate Party. Prime minister since 18 October 2022 and still in office on 4 October 2026.", sv "Parti: Moderaterna. Statsminister sedan den 18 oktober 2022 och fortfarande den 4 oktober 2026." The description no longer mentions the caretaker government; the caretaker status is kept only in the selection, the method and this log. The sources' usedFor and the licensing were rewritten to agree. The Riksdag's open-data terms were not used because no open-data document for the dismissal was identified. | fixed |
| carl-gustaf-ekman | The English party names in four notes (carl-gustaf-ekman, felix-hamrin: Freeminded People's Party; axel-pehrsson-bramstorp: Farmers' League; ola-ullsten: People's Party) came from the English Wikipedia, a verification source; similarly Hammarskjöld's "No party (independent)" / "Partilös" against Wikidata's "högervilde". | Right as to how the first draft was made (the method said so). Wikidata (query 19) still has no English label for Q4887122, Q110472693 or Q53764745. The names were kept but re-based: each is a literal translation of the Wikidata Swedish label (frisinnade folkpartiet, bondeförbundet, folkpartiet), and the English Wikipedia only confirms that the translation is the established English name; a party name is a short name, not protected expression. This is stated as an explicit point in the licensing, in the method, and in the locator of each card's English Wikipedia evidence. The comparison was re-implemented as a self-contained script, published verbatim as query 17 and run on the saved page and Wikidata result: 45 entries, 35 names, every back equal. Query 15 now says the original scripts were not kept. | fixed |
